The weekly meeting has become ninety minutes of people reading their updates aloud.

Half the agenda could be a written document, and the engineers keep their cameras off and work on other tickets.

Last Monday we spent seventy minutes on updates and twenty on the one decision that mattered.

That decision, whether to delay the billing migration, was rushed because the meeting was already over time.

So the agenda is upside down: the thing that needs the whole room gets the least of it.

What I want to try is a three-line written update by Friday: what changed, what is blocked, what decision you need.

Then the Monday meeting is for decisions and disagreements only, and if there is no decision on the agenda, we cancel it.

The managers will miss the meeting where they feel informed, and that is a real cost worth naming.

But a meeting that exists to make people feel informed is a meeting nobody is allowed to skip, and that is the problem.
